blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Visual context is a powerful cue for object recognition: scenes inform what, where, and at what scale objects are likely to appear. Yet over-reliance on context becomes a failure mode when models predict objects based on their typical neighbors rather than the objects' own visual features, which we call typicality bias. While extensively studied in the pre-Transformer era, it has often been assumed that architectural and scale improvements would naturally solve it, and a systematic diagnostic across the modern vision stack remains absent. We provide such a diagnostic framework. We measure typicality bias via normalized pointwise mutual information (NPMI) over object pairs, and introduce STRANGE-Bench (Synthetic Typicality-RANked Grounded Evaluation Benchmark): a photorealistic, layout-controlled benchmark spanning 17 sub-tiers from typical to never-co-occurring object pairs. Across five model families (specialist detectors, open-vocabulary detectors, self-supervised, vision-language, and multimodal large language models) and three recognition tasks (supervised detection, open-vocabulary detection, and classification), the bias is prevalent: gaps of 5-11 p.p. persist when objects appear outside their typical company, and do not consistently shrink with scale. To mitigate it, we turn to data augmentation: existing augmentations are designed for visual diversity, not for breaking co-occurrence shortcuts, and sample from the very distribution that produces typicality bias. We propose Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS), a simple sampling rule for paste-based augmentations that uses the NPMI signal to tilt the training-time co-occurrence distribution toward atypical partners. AAS reduces the typicality gap by up to 1.6 p.p. on natural-image COCO splits and 23.0 p.p. on synthetic STRANGE-Bench across three model families, without sacrificing overall performance.
blocks.zh: 视觉上下文是物体识别的有力提示:场景告知物体可能出现的内容、地点和规模。 然而过度依赖上下文却成为了一种失败模式,当模型根据物体的典型邻接而不是物体自身的视觉特征来预测物体,我们称之为典型偏差. 虽然在过渡前时代进行了广泛的研究,但人们常常认为建筑和规模的改进会自然地解决它,而整个现代视觉堆积的系统诊断仍然缺失. 我们提供了这样一个诊断框架。 我们通过对对象对的常态化点相信息(NPMI)来测量典型性偏差,并引入了STRANGE-Bench(Synthetic Classicity-RANed Grounded Evaluation Birgin):一个从典型对到永不同时发生的17个子级的光现实性,布局控制的基准. 5个模范家庭(专业探测器、开放式活道探测器、自我监督、视觉语言和多模式大型语言模型)和3个识别任务(监督探测、开放式活道探测和分类)的偏差很普遍:当物体出现在其典型公司之外时,5-11p.的空隙就持续存在,而且不会随规模而持续收缩。 为了缓解它,我们转向数据增强: 现有的增强是为了视觉多样性而设计的,而不是为了打破共同发生的捷径, 以及来自产生典型偏差的分布的样本。 我们提出Anchor-非典型抽样(AAS),这是基于粘贴的增强的简单抽样规则,利用国家预防暴力倡议的信号,将培训时间同步分布向非典型伙伴倾斜。 AAS在自然成像COCO分出上将典型差距缩小到1.6p.p.,在合成STRANGE-Bench上缩小到23.0p.,跨越了三个模型家族,同时不牺牲整体性能.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Modern recognition models are trained on large-scale datasets of natural images. Such images capture objects in their typical surroundings, e.g. , a cow on grass, a boat in water, or a stove in a kitchen. These models can exploit co-occurrence cues that go unnoticed on standard benchmarks, since training and test sets draw from the same patterns. Failures surface only when objects appear in atypical contexts, e.g. , a cow on a beach [ 3 ] . While context is itself informative for recognition [ 48 , 35 ] , models can come to use it as a shortcut around the object’s visual features. This over-reliance on co-occurring context has been studied through context-based interventions [ 43 , 45 , 12 , 40 ] , controlled benchmarks [ 31 , 38 , 27 ] , and dedicated out-of-context detection [ 1 , 7 ] . All these studies converge on the same conclusion: classifiers exploit co-occurrence shortcuts and fail when they are absent.
blocks.zh: 现代识别模型对自然影像的大规模数据集进行了培训. 这种图像捕捉其典型周围的物体,例如草地上的牛,水中的船,或厨房中的炉子. 这些模型可以利用在标准基准上不被注意的共同发生提示,因为培训和测试集借鉴了同样的模式。 只有在物体在非典型情况下出现时才会出现故障,例如海滩上的母牛[3]. 虽然上下文本身是用于识别的信息[48,35],但模型可以把它作为围绕对象视觉特征的捷径. 通过基于具体情况的干预[43、45、12、40]、控制下的基准[31、38、27]和专门的校外检测[1、7],研究了过度依赖共同发生的情况。 所有这些研究都得出相同的结论:分类者利用共发生捷径,缺席时失败.

blocks.en: It is unclear whether these findings still hold across the modern vision stack. Recent architectures and training paradigms such as end-to-end detection transformers [ 9 , 61 , 56 ] , open-vocabulary detectors that ground predictions in language [ 30 , 33 , 34 ] , self-supervised vision foundation models [ 11 , 36 , 44 ] , vision-language models pretrained on billions of image-text pairs [ 37 , 14 , 55 , 49 ] , and large multimodal models that fuse vision and language at scale [ 25 ] are expected to alleviate context reliance through enhancements such as deformable attention, language grounding, as well as web-scale data diversity [ 52 , 30 , 37 ] . Recent work has examined whether such shortcuts persist for specific subsets of the stack: segmentation and detection through explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods [ 16 ] , and nuisance-based robustness benchmarks [ 58 , 17 ] . However, a systematic diagnostic across diverse model families that evaluates on object pairs never co-occurring in natural data remains underexplored.
blocks.zh: 尚不清楚这些结论是否仍然贯穿现代视野。 近期的架构和培训范式,如端对端检测变压器[9,61,56],地面预测语言[30,33,34],自控视觉基础模型[11,36,44],视觉语言模型预训数十亿影像文字对[37,14,55,49],以及大规模融合视觉和语言的大型多式联运模型[25],预计将通过变形关注,语言定位,以及网络尺度数据多样性等增强,减轻对背景的依赖[52,30,37]. 最近的工作审查了这种捷径是否对堆叠的特定子集继续存在:通过可解释的人工智能方法进行分割和检测[16],以及基于骚扰的强性基准[58,17]。 但是,对自然数据中从未共同出现的对对象对进行评价的各种不同模范家庭的系统诊断仍然没有得到充分探讨。

blocks.en: In this work, we revisit this phenomenon systematically and at scale across modern vision models. We refer to it as typicality bias : the tendency of recognition models to base predictions on familiar co-occurring context rather than the target object’s own visual evidence. As shown in Fig. 1 , a model exhibiting typicality bias performs well when objects appear in typical contexts and degrades when they appear alone or in atypical contexts.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们系统和大规模地在现代愿景模型中重新审视这一现象。 我们称之为典型偏差:识别模型倾向于根据熟悉的共同发生情况而不是目标对象自己的视觉证据进行预测。 如图1所示,一个显示典型性偏差的模型在物体出现于典型情况下时表现良好,在物体单独出现或非典型情况下则退化。

blocks.en: To diagnose typicality bias systematically, we introduce a framework based on normalized pointwise mutual information (NPMI) over object pairs. For each anchor class, we use NPMI to construct paired evaluation splits in which the anchor (object category under examination) appears alongside either typical or atypical partners. To extend this natural-data evaluation with co-occurrence regimes that natural data do not cover (see Fig. 2 ), we further release STRANGE-Bench ( S ynthetic T ypicality- RAN ked G rounded E valuation Bench mark), a photorealistic, layout-controlled synthetic benchmark spanning the full spectrum from typical to never-co-occurring object pairs.
blocks.zh: 为了系统地判断典型性偏差,我们引入了一个基于对对象对的常点互通信息(NPMI)的框架. 对于每个锚类,我们利用国家防范机制来构建配对评价分割,其中锚(正在审查的对象类别)与典型或非典型的伙伴一起出现。 为了将这种自然数据评价与自然数据未覆盖的共发生系统(见图2)相扩展,我们进一步发布了STRAngE-Bench(Synthetic T ypicality-RAN ked G rounded E valuation Bench mark),这是一个光现实主义的,布局控制的合成基准,从典型的对对象到永不同时发生的对对象.

blocks.en: A complementary question is how to mitigate typicality bias. Data augmentation is a natural lever for this, since it directly shapes the training distribution that produces the bias. In practice, existing augmentations are designed to add visual diversity, not to break co-occurrence shortcuts: both non-generative [ 6 , 57 , 21 ] and generative [ 59 , 24 , 53 ] methods sample from the natural training distribution, preserving rather than perturbing it. We present the first systematic study of how popular data augmentations interact with typicality bias across representative model families, and propose a simple context-aware sampling rule that reduces the bias while preserving overall accuracy.
blocks.zh: 一个补充问题是如何减少典型的偏差。 数据增强是这方面的一个天然杠杆,因为它直接塑造了产生偏差的训练分布. 在实践中,现有的增强法旨在增加视觉多样性,而不是打破共同发生的捷径:既非遗传性[6,57,21],又来自自然训练分布的遗传性[59,24,53]方法样本,保存而非扰动. 我们介绍了关于大众数据增益如何与代表性模型家族的典型偏差相互作用的第一次系统研究,并提出了一种简单的上下文意识抽样规则,在保持整体准确性的同时减少偏差。

blocks.en: Our findings reveal three patterns. First, typicality bias persists across diverse model families and tasks, with gaps of 𝟓 \mathbf{5} – 𝟏𝟏 \mathbf{11} p.p. between typical and atypical splits. Second , the bias does not consistently shrink with scale: more pretraining data does not narrow the gap, and larger models narrow it without closing it, indicating that scale alone is not a solution. Third , most non-paste augmentations leave the gap largely unchanged or narrow it by lowering both sides, while paste-based ones narrow it on STRANGE-Bench. AAS lifts atypical scenes further without hurting typical ones, and reduces the gap of standard training by up to 1.6 \mathbf{1.6} p.p. on natural-image COCO [ 29 ] splits and 23.0 \mathbf{23.0} p.p. on synthetic STRANGE-Bench, without sacrificing overall performance.
blocks.zh: 我们的调查结果揭示了三种模式。 首先,在不同的模范家庭和任务中,典型的偏差持续存在,在典型和非典型的分裂之间差距为 5\ mathbf{5} – 11\ mathbf{11} p.p. 第二,偏差不会随尺度而持续缩小:更多的预训数据不会缩小差距,更大的模型在不关闭的情况下缩小差距,表明尺度本身并不是一个解决方案. 第三,大多数非粘贴增强剂通过降低两侧而使差距基本保持不变或缩小,而以粘贴为主的则在STRANGE-Bench上缩小. AAS将非典型场景进一步提升而不会伤害典型场景,并将标准训练的差距缩小至1.6\ mathbf{1.6} p.p. 关于自然图像COCO [29] 拆分和23.0\mathbf{23.0} p.p.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows:
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献概述如下:

blocks.en: 1. Typicality bias persists across the modern vision stack. We provide a unified diagnostic of typicality bias spanning five model families (specialist detection, open-vocabulary detection, self-supervised representations, vision-language models, and multimodal LLMs) and three recognition tasks. Our key finding is that typicality bias persists across diverse tasks and scales. 2. A photorealistic synthetic benchmark for tiered typicality. We present STRANGE-Bench , a layout-controlled synthetic benchmark spanning the full spectrum from typical to never-co-occurring object pairs, enabling controlled evaluation in low-NPMI regimes that natural data cannot cover; blinded user studies confirm that its gaps are not rendering artifacts. 3. Anchor-Atypicality Sampling for mitigation. We present the first systematic study of how popular data augmentations interact with typicality bias across representative model families, and propose Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS), a simple sampling rule for paste-based augmentation that reduces typicality bias while preserving overall performance.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 典型的偏差在现代视觉堆栈中持续存在。 我们对跨越五个模范家庭的典型性偏差(专家检测、公开投票检测、自我监督的表述、视觉语言模型和多式联运有限责任公司)和三项识别任务进行统一诊断。 我们的主要发现是,不同任务和规模的典型性偏见依然存在。 2. 分层典型的光现实性合成基准。 我们提出STRANGE-Bench,一种布局控制的合成基准,从典型的对对象到永不交织的对对象,能够在自然数据无法覆盖的低NPMI系统中进行控制评价;盲目的用户研究证实,其差距不是在制造文物。 3. 非典型性 采样以缓解. 我们介绍了关于大众数据增强如何与代表性模式家庭的典型性偏差相互作用的第一次系统研究,并提出了Anchor-非典型性抽样(AAS),这是基于粘贴的增强的简单抽样规则,在保持整体性能的同时减少典型性偏差。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Contextual and co-occurrence bias in recognition models. Reliance on co-occurring context as a predictive shortcut is well-documented for older architectures, but less so for the modern stack. Causal interventions demonstrate the dependence by manipulating features or inputs: via causal inpainting on convolutional neural network (CNN) features [ 43 ] , and via feature-space splitting on COCO-Stuff [ 8 , 45 ] . Out-of-context benchmarks measure model behavior when objects appear in atypical scenes [ 1 , 7 ] . Concept-graph approaches discover and mitigate co-occurrence biases via concept-graph clique sampling [ 12 ] or open-set foundation-model tagging [ 40 ] .
More recent work has examined context bias in modern models, but only in narrower settings: XAI for segmentation and detection [ 16 ] , nuisance-based robustness benchmarks [ 58 ] , referring expression generation [ 32 ] , and compositional action recognition [ 2 ] .
In contrast to these narrower studies, we apply one diagnostic across five model families, complemented by STRANGE-Bench , which covers co-occurrence regimes absent from natural data, and we also test mitigations.
blocks.zh:
认识模型中的背景和共同发生的偏差。 依赖共同发生的上下文作为预测捷径,对于较古老的建筑来说是有充分记载的,但对现代堆栈来说则较少. 因果关系干预通过操纵特征或输入来证明依赖性:通过因果涂抹转录神经网络特征[43],并通过在COCO-Stuff上分割特征空间[8,45]. 文本外基准测量非典型场景中出现物体时的模型行为[1,7]. 概念图方法通过概念图群抽样[12]或开放式的基建模型标记[40]发现并减轻共同发生的偏差。
最近的工作审查了现代模型的背景偏差,但只在较窄的环境下: XAI用于分割和检测[16],基于扰动的强性基准[58],参考表达生成[32],以及组成动作识别[2].
与这些较狭义的研究相反,我们用一个诊断方法对五个模式家庭进行诊断,并辅之以STRANGE-Bench, 涵盖自然数据中缺失的共发性制度,我们还测试缓解措施。

blocks.en:
Data augmentation for visual recognition. Data augmentation shapes the training distribution that models see, but existing methods were not designed with co-occurrence shortcuts in mind. Non-generative methods perturb individual images (flip, crop, color jitter) or stitch existing instances together (MixUp [ 57 ] , Mosaic [ 6 ] , Simple Copy-Paste [ 21 ] ). Generative methods synthesize new instances using text-to-image diffusion (XPaste [ 59 ] , InstanceAug [ 24 ] , MosaicFusion [ 53 ] ). Across both families (see Table 1 ), pasted or generated instances are sampled from the natural co-occurrence distribution. Whether this preserves typicality bias, and whether targeted modifications can reduce it, have not been systematically studied. We present such a study on representative model families, and
propose Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS) , a sampling rule that plugs into any paste-based augmentation and reduces typicality bias while preserving overall performance.
blocks.zh:
数据增强用于视觉识别. 数据增强塑造了模型所看到的训练分布,但现有方法的设计并没有考虑到共同发生的捷径. 非遗传方法扰动个体图像(flip, crop, color jitter)或将已有实例缝合在一起(MixUp [57], Mosaic [6], 简单复制[21]). 基因方法利用文本到图像的传播来合成新的实例(XPaste [59],exampleAug [24],MosaicFusion [53] ). 在两个家庭中(见表1),根据自然同时发生的分布对粘贴或生成的例子进行了抽样。 这种做法是否保留了典型性偏差,以及有针对性的修改是否能够减少这种偏差,都没有得到系统的研究. 我们提出了关于有代表性的模范家庭的这种研究报告,以及
提出Anchor-非典型采样(AAS),一种在保持整体性能的同时插入任何基于粘贴的增强并减少典型偏差的采样规则.

blocks.en: Modern visual recognition models. The vision recognition stack has evolved rapidly along architectural and supervision axes. Specialist detection transformers such as DETR [ 9 ] , Deformable DETR [ 60 ] , and Co-DETR/Co-DINO [ 61 ] formulate detection end-to-end via (deformable) attention. Open-vocabulary detectors such as GLIP [ 26 ] and Grounding DINO [ 30 ] extend detection to text-conditioned localization. Self-supervised foundation models such as DINOv2 [ 36 ] and DINOv3 [ 44 ] learn general-purpose visual representations from hundreds of millions of unlabeled images. Vision–language models (CLIP [ 37 ] , OpenCLIP [ 14 ] ) and large multimodal models (LLaVA-OneVision [ 25 ] ) use web-scale image–text pretraining for zero-shot recognition and image understanding. Each of these design choices, from deformable attention focusing on object regions to language grounding and web-scale data diversity, is expected to be resistant to context shortcuts. Yet none is trained or evaluated with such shortcuts in mind, leaving their susceptibility to typicality bias underexamined, a gap our diagnostic, benchmark, and mitigation directly address.
blocks.zh: 现代视觉识别模型. 视觉识别堆沿建筑和监理轴快速发展. 专家检测变压器如DETR [9],变形DETR [60],以及Co-DETR/Co-DINO [61]通过(变形)注意来制备检测端到端. GLIP [26] 和Grounding DINO [30] 等开放式伏波探测器将探测扩展到文本条件本地化. DINOv2[36]和DINOv3[44]等自我监督的基础模型从数亿无标签图像中学习通用视觉表现. blocks.en: 3 Diagnosing and Mitigating Typicality Bias
blocks.zh: 3 诊断和减轻典型现象

blocks.en: In this section, we present a framework for diagnosing and mitigating typicality bias, built around normalized pointwise mutual information (NPMI). We first use NPMI to construct paired typical and atypical evaluation splits on real images (Sec. 3.1 ). To probe co-occurrence regimes that real data cannot reach, we then introduce STRANGE-Bench , a layout-grounded synthetic benchmark spanning 17 sub-tiers from natural co-occurrence to never-co-occurring object pairs (Sec. 3.2 ). Finally, we present Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS) , a sampling rule for paste-based augmentations that perturbs training-time co-occurrence using the same NPMI signal (Sec. 3.3 ). STRANGE-Bench is an evaluation instrument and AAS a training-time intervention.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们提出一个诊断和减轻典型偏差的框架,这个框架是围绕常态点性相互信息(NPMI)建立的。 我们首先使用国家防范机制在真实图像上构建成对的典型和非典型的评价分裂(第3.1条)。 为了探究真实数据无法达到的共发现象,我们引入了STRANGE-Bench——一个布局基础合成基准,从自然共发现象到永不发生现象的物体对共发现象(第3.2条)。 最后,我们介绍了Anchor-非典型抽样(AAS),这是使用相同的国家防范机制信号(第3.3节)干扰培训时间共同发生的基于粘贴的增强的取样规则。 STRANGE-Bench是一个评估工具,AAS是一个培训时间干预.

blocks.en: 3.1 NPMI Diagnostic on Natural Data
blocks.zh: 3.1 自然数据诊断

blocks.en: To quantify typicality bias on real data, we measure how a model’s behavior changes between paired scenes where an anchor class (the target object category we examine) appears alongside its typical co-occurrence partners versus its atypical ones. This requires a typicality measure that is comparable across object categories of widely different frequencies, since we aggregate gaps over all anchor classes ( e.g. , person co-occurs with almost everything, while toaster with almost nothing). We use normalized pointwise mutual information (NPMI), which is bounded in [ − 1 , 1 ] [-1,1] and corrects for marginal class frequency, making typicality directly comparable across rare and common categories.
blocks.zh: 为了量化真实数据上的典型偏差,我们衡量一个模型的行为如何在成对的场景之间发生变化,在这些场景中,锚类(我们所审查的目标对象类别)与典型的共性伙伴相对照。 这就需要一种典型的度量标准,在频率大不相同的对象类别之间可以比较,因为我们将所有锚类(例如,人与人之间几乎什么都有,而烤面包机几乎一无所有)的缺口汇总在一起. 我们使用正常的点性相互信息(NPMI),它以[− 1, 1] [-1,1] 为限,并纠正边缘类频率,使典型性在罕见和常见类别之间直接可比.

blocks.en: Paired typical/atypical splits. For each anchor class c c , we build paired evaluation splits. Both splits contain images where c c is present alongside at least one partner, such that typical partners appear only in one split and atypical partners only in the other. Concretely, for anchor c c and a quantile parameter α ∈ ( 0 , 0.5 ) \alpha\in(0,0.5) , we define typical and atypical partner sets via per-anchor NPMI quantiles: 𝒩 typ ​ ( c ) = { j : NPMI ​ ( c , j ) ≥ q 1 − α ( c ) } , 𝒩 aty ​ ( c ) = { j : NPMI ​ ( c , j ) ≤ q α ( c ) } , \mathcal{N}^{\text{typ}}(c)=\{\,j:\text{NPMI}(c,j)\geq q_{1-\alpha}^{(c)}\,\},\qquad\mathcal{N}^{\text{aty}}(c)=\{\,j:\text{NPMI}(c,j)\leq q_{\alpha}^{(c)}\,\}, (2) where q p ( c ) q_{p}^{(c)} is the p p -quantile of NPMI in row c c , restricted to partners with sufficient train-set co-occurrence with c c . 1 1 1 Specifically, typical candidates require N i ​ j ≥ 5 N_{ij}\geq 5 ; atypical candidates require N i ​ j ≥ 1 N_{ij}\geq 1 and at least one val image containing both c c and j j , and the atypical quantile is taken over these candidates. The count floors keep wide quantile cuts on noisy long-tail rows from drifting into the neutral region. Per-anchor quantiles, rather than a fixed top- K K , calibrate each anchor’s partner set to its own NPMI distribution: a fixed K K would over-include partners for common anchors (which have many high-NPMI pairs) and under-include for rare ones. The choice of α \alpha trades partner-set sharpness against split sample size. A val image I I joins the Typical split for c c iff c ∈ I c\in I , I ∩ 𝒩 typ ​ ( c ) ≠ ∅ I\cap\mathcal{N}^{\text{typ}}(c)\neq\emptyset , and I ∩ 𝒩 aty ​ ( c ) = ∅ I\cap\mathcal{N}^{\text{aty}}(c)=\emptyset (and symmetrically for the Atypical split). This scene-purity requirement prevents typical and atypical partners from leaking across splits when an image contains both. The choice of α \alpha , the val-coverage floor for long-tail anchors, and additional implementation details are provided in Appendix B.2 . Figure 2 shows the NPMI matrix used here, alongside example scenes from STRANGE-Bench at representative NPMI tiers; we describe its construction next.

blocks.en: The diagnostic in Sec. 3.1 covers only the portion of the NPMI spectrum that exists in natural data, i.e. , pairs from typical (high NPMI) to atypical (low NPMI). It cannot reach pairs that never co-occur in training, where NPMI is undefined and no natural images exist. Nor can it vary contextual load while controlling for typicality, since natural images do not allow for adding or removing partners. To examine these regimes, we build STRANGE-Bench ( S ynthetic T ypicality- RAN ked G rounded E valuation Bench mark), a layout-grounded photorealistic benchmark of 5,523 5{,}523 scenes with 17,332 17{,}332 annotations across 17 sub-tiers (see Fig. 3 ). Each scene contains an anchor category and k ∈ { 0 , … , 5 } k\in\{0,\dots,5\} partners, all uniformly typical or atypical with respect to the anchor. We call k k the contextual load and a ( k k , typicality) cell a tier : T 1 T_{1} to T 6 T_{6} cover k = 0 k=0 to 5 5 ( T 1 T_{1} varies only the background), and App. C.3 lists every sub-tier. k ≤ 4 k\leq 4 covers 91 % 91\% of COCO train2017 images; k k is set by design rather than matched to natural statistics. A separate T never T_{\text{never}} tier pairs the anchor with categories that never co-occur with it in COCO train2017 ; atypical tiers also contain such pairs, but T never T_{\text{never}} requires every pair in the scene, partners included, to have zero co-occurrences. This sweeps bias as a function of both typicality and contextual load.

blocks.en: Generation pipeline. Each scene is generated by a five-stage pipeline (Fig. 3 ) that turns a set of categories into an annotated photorealistic image. (1) Typicality-based sampling. For a target sub-tier, we sample an anchor and k k partners from the COCO label set, preferring partners with high NPMI (typical arm) or low NPMI (atypical arm) with the anchor and with each other (App. C.3 ). (2) Layout and caption. A Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct [ 54 ] planner (or, for 21 % 21\% of the scenes, a rule-based solver) places the categories in a bounding-box layout and writes from it one wide-shot caption that names every object with its position in the image; the renderer sees the layout only through this caption. The caption asks for a minimalist scene with every object fully visible, which targets the two failure modes of our pilot renders: cropped objects and unprompted clutter. (3) Rendering and annotation. Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large [ 46 , 18 ] renders the caption, and SAM3 [ 10 ] segments each intended category from a text prompt ( e.g. , “a giraffe”); the boxes of its instance masks become the annotations. We render up to three times and keep the first render in which SAM3 finds every intended category ( 89.5 % 89.5\% of the categories are found on the first render, 95.9 % 95.9\% within three). (4) Audit. An object that was not asked for would turn its detections into false positives and could bring typical context into an atypical scene. A Grounding DINO [ 30 ] auditor therefore rejects scenes with unintended or duplicate objects, and a second audit with SAM3 and OWLv2 [ 34 ] turns each remaining one into an ignore region, where predictions are not counted, or drops the scene if it is atypical and the object co-occurs with an intended category more often than chance (NPMI > 0 >0 ). (5) Assembly. Scenes that miss an intended category are dropped, and the typical and atypical sub-tiers at each k k are cut to the same size; 44.6 % 44.6\% of the rendered scenes enter STRANGE-Bench. Prompt templates, audit thresholds, the per-tier composition, and the yield of each stage are provided in Appendix C .

blocks.en: 3.3 Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS)
blocks.zh: 3.3 锚-非典型取样(AAS)

blocks.en: Standard Copy-Paste [ 21 ] and X-Paste [ 59 ] sample paste classes uniformly (or by inverse frequency), so the trained co-occurrence distribution mirrors the source distribution and reinforces typicality bias. AAS replaces uniform sampling with an anchor-conditioned, atypicality-tilted distribution that shifts the training-time joint toward low-NPMI pairs while preserving overall class coverage.
blocks.zh: 标准Copy-Paste [21] 和X-Paste [59] 样本粘贴类统一(或通过反向频率),因此训练的共聚分布镜像源分布,强化典型偏差. AAS用锚定的、非典型的分布取代统一取样,将培训时间的联合型改为低-NPMI配对型,同时保持整体班级覆盖。

blocks.en: AAS explicitly perturbs the training-time NPMI structure: the model sees anchors paired with their bottom-NPMI partners far more often than the natural distribution would allow. This directly attacks the shortcut behind typicality bias (“predict j j because a a is present”) by making that shortcut unreliable during training. Since the tilt is anchor-conditional rather than global, typical co-occurrences in the original data are largely preserved, so the intervention is asymmetric: gap-closing without overall-performance regression.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: In this section, we evaluate typicality bias across the modern vision stack and study its mitigation. We first provide our experimental setup in Sec. 4.1 , including datasets, evaluation metrics, models, and augmentation suites. We then survey five model families on the COCO NPMI splits and the synthetic STRANGE-Bench in Sec. 4.2 , establishing that the bias persists across the stack and does not consistently shrink with scale. We finally run the systematic mitigation study on three representative families in Sec. 4.3 , showing that AAS reduces the typicality gap while preserving overall performance. Sec. 4.4 checks with human raters that the gaps come from the models and not from the rendered scenes.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们评价整个现代视觉堆栈的典型性偏差,并研究其缓解. 我们首先在第4.1节中提供我们的实验设置,包括数据集,评价度量衡,模型和增强套件. 然后,我们调查了5个模范家庭的COCO NPALI分裂和合成的STRANGE-Bench sec. 4.2, 确定该偏差在堆积层中持续存在,不会随着规模而不断缩小。 我们最终在4.3节对三个有代表性的家庭进行了系统的缓解研究,表明AAS在保持总体性能的同时缩小了典型性差距. 第4.4节与人类检测员核对,发现差距来自模型,而不是场景。

blocks.en:
Models. We evaluate typicality bias on a representative model from each of five families spanning the modern vision stack: specialist detection (Co-DINO [ 61 ] R-50, Swin-L), open-vocabulary detection (Grounding DINO [ 30 ] Swin-B), self-supervised classification (DINOv3 [ 44 ] ViT-B, both linear-probe and fine-tuned), vision–language models (CLIP [ 37 ] ViT-B/16, OpenCLIP [ 14 ] ViT-B/16 LAION-2B), and multimodal LLMs (LLaVA-OneVision-7B [ 25 ] ).
For the diagnostic survey, we use the public pretrained checkpoints officially released by the authors. These families span the modern vision stack along two axes: supervision regime (fully supervised, language-grounded, self-supervised, contrastive image–text, and instruction-tuned) and pretraining data scale (from ∼ 100 \sim 100 K images for COCO-trained specialists to ∼ 2 \sim 2 billion image–text pairs for OpenCLIP and LLaVA-OneVision). Any persistence of bias across this set is therefore unlikely to be an artifact of a single paradigm or scale.

在诊断调查中,我们使用提交人正式释放的公共预先训练的检查站。 这些家庭沿着两条轴线跨过现代视觉堆栈:监督制度(完全监督、基于语言、自我监督、对比性图像-文本以及指导调整)和预训数据尺度(从CO训练专家的100\sim 100K图像到2\sim 20亿图像-OpenCLIP和LLaVA-One Vision的文本对)。 因此,这一组中持续存在的偏见不可能是单一范式或规模的文物。

blocks.en: For the systematic mitigation study, we select one representative from each of the three task settings, spanning supervision regime, architecture, and task: Co-DINO R-50 (specialist closed-vocabulary detection), Grounding DINO Swin-B (open-vocabulary, text-conditioned), and DINOv3 ViT-B/16 fine-tuned (SSL foundational backbone fine-tuned for classification). All representative models are trained on COCO train2017 (initialized from the public pretrained checkpoints) under the augmentation variants below. Full training recipes, checkpoint sources, hyperparameters, and compute budgets are provided in Appendix B.1 . We leave vision–language models and multimodal LLMs out of the mitigation study, since their co-occurrence prior is set during web-scale pretraining.
blocks.zh: 为了进行系统的缓解研究,我们从三个任务设置中各自挑选一名代表,涉及监督制度、架构和任务:共同DINO R-50(专业闭路检测)、地面DINO Swin-B(开放式省道,文字条件)和DINOv3 VIT-B/16微调(SSL基础骨干进行分类微调)。 所有具有代表性的型号都按照下文的扩编变体在COCO 2017号列车(从公共预先训练的检查站开始)上接受培训. 完整的培训食谱、检查站来源、超参数和计算预算载于附录B.1。 我们不将视觉语言模型和多种模式的LLMs纳入缓解研究,因为这些模型和LLMs在网络规模的前期培训中被设定。

blocks.en:
Augmentation suite. We compare AAS against a representative suite of seven augmentations
spanning two axes, static / dynamic and non-generative / generative : Color jitter , MixUp [ 57 ] , Mosaic [ 6 ] , YOLOX [ 20 ] (MixUp + Mosaic), SCP [ 21 ] , XPaste [ 59 ] , and InstAug [ 24 ] . We additionally report a Std. baseline using only standard augmentation (flip, crop, resize). None of the existing augmentations are designed to break co-occurrence shortcuts; whether they incidentally affect typicality bias is an empirical question we answer below. AAS hyperparameters are selected once on a 25 % 25\% COCO subset and held fixed across architectures and tasks; per-augmentation hyperparameters are detailed in Appendix B.1.4 .

Across all three, AAS preserves overall accuracy, closes
the typicality gap on the majority of (model, eval-split) cells, and
improves extreme-atypical performance the most.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We revisited typicality bias , the tendency of recognition models to anchor predictions on familiar co-occurring context rather than the object itself. Across the modern vision stack, the bias persists across diverse model families and pretraining scales, without consistently shrinking with size. To diagnose it on a continuous scale, we introduced an NPMI-based diagnostic and the photorealistic STRANGE-Bench. To mitigate it, we further proposed Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS), a sampling rule for paste-based augmentation that closes the typicality gap by lifting atypical-context performance without degrading typical-context performance.
blocks.zh: 我们重新审视了典型的偏差,即识别模型将预测定位在熟悉的共同发生情况而不是物体本身上的趋势。 在整个现代愿景堆中,不同模范家庭和预训规模的偏见持续存在,没有随着规模的缩小而不断缩小。 为了持续地诊断它,我们引入了基于国家防范机制的诊断和光现实主义的STRANGE-Bench。 为了缓解这种情况,我们进一步提出了Anchor-Acidentity Sampling(AAS),这是基于粘贴的增强的抽样规则,它通过解除非典型的-context性能而不贬低典型-context性能来弥补典型性差距.

blocks.en: Our diagnostic relies on annotated co-occurrence statistics, and AAS requires training pipelines that allow for paste-based augmentations, leaving contrastive image-text and instruction-following pretraining, where the bias is most pronounced, as open directions for future work. These findings suggest that contextual robustness should be reported alongside in-distribution performance in the standard evaluation of foundation-scale recognition models.
blocks.zh: 我们的诊断依赖于附加说明的共发性统计数据,而AAS需要培训管道,允许基于粘贴的增强,留下对比的图像文本和遵循指导的预训,在偏差最突出的地方,作为未来工作的开放方向. 这些调查结果表明,在对基金会规模识别模型进行标准评价时,应同时报告内部的稳健性。

blocks.en: In this section, we report the full results behind Sec. 4 and further analyses. We first give the full results of each family in App. A.1 to A.4 : the Objects365 cross-domain splits and the per-tier STRANGE-Bench breakdown for the rows of Tabs. 2 to 4 , and the DINOv3 linear probe. We then show the empirical selection of AAS temperature β \beta in App. A.5 and test in App. A.6 whether the gaps and the AAS gains depend on COCO NPMI or on the generator of the benchmark. We finally separate pretraining data from model capacity in App. A.7 , test whether models also rely on the usual spatial arrangement of a pair in App. A.8 , evaluate a target-focused baseline that inpaints the partners away in App. A.9 , and report the spread of the AAS rows over training runs in App. A.10 . The evaluation datasets and paired splits are defined in App. B.1.1 , and the training and evaluation recipes in App. B.1.4 .
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们报告第4节的全部结果和进一步的分析。 我们首先在App.A.1至A.4中给出每个家族的全部结果:Objects365跨域分割和Tabs各行的每层STRANGE-Bench分解. 2到4,还有DINOv3线性探测器. 然后,我们在App. A.5中显示对AAS温度β \β的实证选择,并在App. A.6中显示对差距和AAS收益的测试是取决于COCO NPMI还是取决于基准的生成者。 我们最终将预训数据与App的模型容量分开. A.7,测试模型是否也依赖于App中一对的通常空间安排. A.8,评价App.A.9中对伙伴进行涂抹的目标重点基线,并报告AAS列在App的训练上分布。 A.10. 联合国 App.B.1.1界定了评价数据集和配对拆分,App界定了培训和评价配方。 B.1.4 (中文(简体) ).

blocks.en: We additionally evaluate typicality bias under the linear-probe (LP) protocol on DINOv3 ViT-B/16, where only a linear classification head is trained on top of the frozen pretrained backbone. This isolates the contribution of the backbone’s representations from end-to-end fine-tuning: any gap that survives the LP setup is encoded in the backbone itself and must be read out of features the backbone already provides, while any gap reduction obtained by augmentation must operate purely through the head’s training signal. We restrict the LP study to Std. and three paste augmentations of the FT sweep (§ A.3 ), SCP, XPaste and XPaste + AAS, since the goal of this section is to characterize the ceiling on what augmentation can achieve in the frozen-backbone regime, not to repeat a full sweep. Unlike in the fine-tuned tables, the AAS row here (XPaste + AAS † ) applies AAS sampling over the whole LP schedule rather than as the late stage of Sec. 3.3 , and every row is a single training draw.

blocks.en: Why augmentation hits a ceiling under LP. The residual gap that no LP augmentation closes ( Δ 1 ​ - ​ 5 ≥ 6.0 \Delta_{1\text{-}5}\geq 6.0 , T never ≤ 70.1 T_{\text{never}}\leq 70.1 ) points to the frozen features: DINOv3 is pretrained without labels on about 1.7 1.7 billion images (LVD-1689M [ 44 ] ), and the gap of the Std. probe grows with the pretraining data (DINOv1 19.3 19.3 , DINOv2 21.5 21.5 , DINOv3 23.9 23.9 ; App. A.7 ), which is consistent with co-occurrence structure that is already present in the features. Once the backbone is frozen, the head-only training signal cannot edit those internal representations; it can only re-route how they are linearly combined into class logits. Paste-based methods re-balance the head’s input distribution and lower the gap from 23.9 23.9 to between 6.0 6.0 and 9.2 9.2 ; the remainder may reflect co-occurrence structure that a linear head cannot separate from the pretrained representation. End-to-end FT (§ A.3 ) lets the gradient reach the backbone, so the pasted atypical samples can also change the features; this is consistent with FT’s Δ 1 ​ - ​ 5 = − 0.8 \Delta_{1\text{-}5}=-0.8 for XPaste + AAS versus LP’s 6.0 6.0 for XPaste + AAS † .

blocks.en: We select the AAS atypicality temperature β \beta once via a small ablation and hold the selected value fixed across all model families and full-COCO runs. Tab. 16 reports the sweep on Co-DINO R-50 (AP), trained on the 25 % 25\% subset of COCO train2017 (mini-COCO, 29,571 29{,}571 images), and on DINOv3 ViT-B/16 fine-tuned on full COCO (mAP). β = 3.5 \beta=3.5 achieves the best or second-best score on every metric for both models, simultaneously balancing overall accuracy, in-domain typicality gap, and STRANGE-Bench coverage, and we adopt it for all main-paper experiments.
blocks.zh: 我们通过一个小的衰竭来选择一个 AAS 非典型温度β\β β\β, 并保持所有模型家族的选定值 和全CO运行。 Tab. 16报告了对Co-DINO R-50(AP)的扫射,对2017年COCO列车25%-25%的子集(mini-CO,29,571 29{,}571 图像)进行了培训,对DINov3 VIT-B/16进行了全CO(mAP)的微调。 β = 3.5\beta = 3.5 = 3.5 对两种车型的每个公尺都取得了最佳或次最佳的分数,同时平衡了总体准确度,域内典型差距,以及STRANGE-Bench的覆盖度,我们采纳了所有主纸实验。

blocks.en: Tradeoff intuition. The sampling distribution P ⁡ ( j ∣ a ) ∝ π ⁡ ( j ) ​ exp ⁡ ( β ​ A ​ ( a , j ) ) P(j\mid a)\propto\pi(j)\exp\big(\beta A(a,j)\big) of Sec. 3.3 has two endpoints. At β = 0 \beta=0 , AAS samples paste classes uniformly and independently of the anchor, i.e. the XPaste baseline, and provides no debiasing signal; as β → ∞ \beta\to\infty , AAS concentrates almost all paste mass on the most atypical partners, which over-distorts the training-time joint and starts to hurt typical-pair coverage and overall accuracy. The sweep traces this tradeoff: β = 2 \beta=2 leaves residual gap ( Δ T-A = 8.1 \Delta^{\text{T-A}}=8.1 for Co-DINO, 9.5 9.5 for DINOv3 FT, both worse than β = 3.5 \beta=3.5 ); β = 5 \beta=5 matches or beats β = 3.5 \beta=3.5 on a few metrics (Co-DINO typical AP, DINOv3 Δ 1 ​ - ​ 5 \Delta_{1\text{-}5} on STRANGE-Bench) but drops on others (Co-DINO val AP, DINOv3 val mAP and gap), reflecting the over-tilting regime. β = 3.5 \beta=3.5 sits near the sweet spot for both families.

blocks.en: A.8 Spatial Arrangement as a Typicality Axis
blocks.zh: A.8 空间安排作为典型轴

blocks.en: NPMI scores whether two classes co-occur, not how they are arranged. To test whether models also rely on the usual arrangement of a pair, we measure how stereotyped it is: for each ordered COCO train2017 pair with at least 10 10 co-occurring images, we take the direction from the largest anchor box to the largest partner box in every such image, bin it into eight 45 ∘ 45^{\circ} sectors, and compute the normalized entropy H ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] H\in[0,1] of the histogram. Low H H means one dominant arrangement, such as a rider above a horse. STRANGE-Bench layouts are generated without regard to these arrangements, so a model that relies on them should recognize the anchor less often in stereotyped pairs. We use the single-partner tier T 2 T_{2} (both arms) and the DINOv3 ViT-B linear probe, count an anchor as recognized when its score is at least 0.5 0.5 , and keep pairs with at least two scenes.
blocks.zh: NPAI的分数是两个课是共同的,而不是如何安排。 为了测试模型是否也依赖于一对的通常安排,我们测量它是如何定型的:对于每对订购的COCO2017列车,至少10对共发图像,我们从最大的锚盒到每个这样的图像中最大的伙伴盒的方向,将其嵌入8个45~45~circ}区段,并计算直方图的规范的Entropy H → [0, 1] H\in [0,1]. 低HH表示一种主导安排,如骑手在马之上. STRANGE-Bench的布局是在不考虑这些安排的情况下产生的,因此依赖它们的模型应该较少地识别定型配对中的锚. 我们使用单伙伴级 T 2 T_{2}(双臂)和DINOv3 VIT-B线性探测器,计算一个锚在得分至少0.5时被确认,并保持对数至少有两个场景.

blocks.en: A.9 Partner Masking
blocks.zh: A.9 伙伴面具

blocks.en: Instead of changing which objects appear together, a mitigation can remove the objects around a target. On COCO train2017 images with exactly two classes ( 35,858 35{,}858 of 117,266 117{,}266 ), partner masking picks one class as the anchor, removes the other with a precomputed LaMa [ 47 ] inpainting and keeps only the anchor label; other images are unchanged. We fine-tune DINOv3 ViT-B/16 with it for 20 epochs, the recipe of the submitted runs, and compare it with the Std. run of the same recipe (Tab. 23 ). Partner masking narrows the STRANGE-Bench gap only from 20.0 20.0 to 18.2 18.2 , while the COCO gap widens from 4.8 4.8 to 5.2 5.2 and both T never T_{\text{never}} ( 67.2 → 65.8 67.2\rightarrow 65.8 ) and COCO val ( 80.9 → 80.1 80.9\rightarrow 80.1 ) drop. A model learns the partners it is shown with each anchor. Partner masking shrinks that set, since the anchor is now often seen alone, so an anchor among atypical partners at test time remains unlike the training images; paste-based augmentation (Sec. 4.3 ) widens the set instead. The invariance to context comes from varying the context, not from deleting it.

blocks.en: The eval suite combines one full-COCO baseline [ 29 ] , four COCO/Objects365 [ 42 ] paired splits, and STRANGE-Bench (Tab. 25 ). The four paired splits are constructed as in § B.2 : per-anchor ranking by COCO train2017 NPMI, applied to val images, quintile cut for the headline ( α = 0.2 \alpha=0.2 ) and decile for an additional ablation ( α = 0.1 \alpha=0.1 ); the typical side is down-sampled per-anchor to approximately match the atypical-side image count. O365 splits apply the same construction, with the same COCO train2017 NPMI matrix, to Objects365 v2 val images whose 365 classes are mapped onto the 80 COCO classes ( 69 69 direct name matches, 11 11 approximate). The cross-domain tables (Tabs. 6 , 9 and 11 ) add a fifth paired split, a third one on O365: the quintile construction on the same val images with the NPMI matrix recomputed on O365 train ( 1,699,452 1{,}699{,}452 images) and the partner vocabulary restricted to the COCO/O365 overlap, i.e. the same 80 80 mapped classes ( 4,349 / 3,834 4{,}349/3{,}834 typical-matched / atypical images, 76 76 anchors). Its partner sets overlap those of the COCO-NPMI split with a mean per-anchor Jaccard index of 0.64 0.64 (typical) and 0.44 0.44 (atypical). Detection runs against full annotations on every split. STRANGE-Bench is reported in the balanced variant (typical and atypical sub-tiers of a tier cut to the same size; 5,523 5{,}523 images across 17 sub-tiers, 11 of them in the main tables); per-tier composition, generation pipeline, and audit are in § C .

blocks.en: Image balancing. After the partner-eligibility filters above, the typical and atypical sides of each cut are highly imbalanced in the natural distribution: typical pairs are roughly an order of magnitude more common than atypical ones, so the unfiltered typical-side image pool is much larger than the atypical-side pool (e.g., 3,501 3{,}501 vs. 389 389 at the quintile cut). To prevent this asymmetry from biasing per-anchor AP estimates, we keep the atypical side intact (it is already the bottleneck) and down-sample the typical side per-anchor so that, for each anchor class, the number of typical-matched images is approximately equal to the number of atypical images for that anchor. The resulting post-balancing counts are reported in Table 30 and feed directly into the eval suite of § B.1.1 .

blocks.en: Why is natural data not enough? Even at the standard cuts we use, the COCO paired-real splits comprise only 465 / 389 465/389 typical-matched / atypical images at the quintile cut ( α = 0.2 \alpha=0.2 ) and 300 / 259 300/259 at the decile ( α = 0.1 \alpha=0.1 ) (Tab. 30 and Tab. 25 ), spread across 64 64 and 61 61 anchor classes. Per-anchor coverage is therefore modest in absolute terms and very uneven across the long tail; anchors whose atypical partners never appear with them in val are dropped ( 16 16 of 80 80 at the quintile cut), and 28 28 of the remaining 64 64 anchors have fewer than three atypical images. More fundamentally, no natural cut can reach the regime where partners never co-occur with the anchor. As Fig. 7 shows, on train2017 the never-co-occur cells form a small minority of the 80 × 80 80\times 80 NPMI matrix ( 982 982 of the 6,320 6{,}320 off-diagonal cells, 15.5 % 15.5\% ), but on val2017 the empty fraction jumps to 49.1 % 49.1\% : nearly half of all category pairs that we might want to probe simply have no images in val. The empty-cell rate is highest in the long-tail × \times long-tail quadrant ( 78.5 % 78.5\% vs. 39.5 % 39.5\% elsewhere), exactly where typicality bias should be most pronounced and stress-tests are most informative. By construction, no quantile cut on val can recover these cells, and the never-co-occur regime ( T never T_{\text{never}} ) is inaccessible from natural data altogether. This is the gap STRANGE-Bench (§ C ) is designed to close: rendering scenes from sampled category sets lets us produce paired typical / atypical scenes and a clean T never T_{\text{never}} tier with balanced per-anchor coverage that natural validation sets structurally cannot offer.

blocks.en: Generality and Extensibility. The pipeline above is deliberately recipe-driven and not COCO-specific. Swapping the input label vocabulary (here, the 80 80 COCO classes) and the source co-occurrence statistics (here, NPMI on COCO train2017 ) is sufficient to generate a STRANGE-Bench-style probe for any other dataset or task family. We release dataset, code, samples, and the Croissant manifest (Tab. 32 ) under a permissive license so the community can: • regenerate STRANGE-Bench at higher resolution or larger scale, • target alternative vocabularies (LVIS [ 22 ] , Objects365 [ 42 ] , fine-grained categories, video frames), • substitute newer generative models (e.g., higher-resolution SD variants [ 46 ] , Imagen [ 39 ] , FLUX [ 5 ] ) or stronger auditors as they appear, and • compose with new typicality axes (action-object, scene-object, temporal context). The pipeline’s modular form (layout, render, segment, audit) means each stage can be replaced independently without rebuilding the rest. Our intent is to provide both a benchmark and a reusable construction recipe for stress-testing co-occurrence shortcuts in vision systems.

blocks.en: Three checks test the typicality structure and two nuisance variables, object scale and position. (i) Tier semantics. Per-tier intended-pair NPMI on COCO-train separates the typical and atypical sub-tiers at every quartile: the lower quartile of every typical sub-tier is at least + 0.05 +0.05 and the upper quartile of every atypical sub-tier at most − 0.20 -0.20 (typical means + 0.18 +0.18 to + 0.24 +0.24 , atypical − 0.27 -0.27 to − 0.31 -0.31 ; pairs that never co-occur have no NPMI and are left out; Fig. 16 ). (ii) Object-scale balance. Median relative bbox area within typical/atypical pairs at fixed k k is matched to within 0.15 0.15 – 0.66 0.66 pt for k = 1 , … , 5 k\!=\!1,\dots,5 (Fig. 17 ); the largest gap is at k = 1 k\!=\!1 ( 0.66 0.66 pt), and the single anchor of T 1 T_{1} is 3.0 3.0 pt larger on the natural than on the atypical background. (iii) Spatial layout. Box centers sit below the image center on average in every sub-tier (mean vertical position 0.60 0.60 to 0.67 0.67 of the image height, 0 0 at the top), and the typical and atypical sub-tiers at the same k k match within 0.013 0.013 in mean position (Fig. 18 ), so the two arms share the same center bias.

and discard the scene if a Grounding DINO [ 30 ] auditor flags extras or duplicates, or if the second audit or the completeness check of Stage 5 fails. Numeric hyperparameters for every stage are deferred to C.6 .

blocks.en:
Limitations. (i) Synthetic eval coverage. STRANGE-Bench reflects SD 3.5L’s rendering distribution and is best read as a paired comparison instrument alongside natural-image evaluation, not in place of it. (ii) Vocabulary scope. Both the diagnostic and STRANGE-Bench operate on COCO- 80 80 as it is important to study on a manageable scale to exactly quantify typicality bias. Richer vocabularies (long-tail and fine-grained categories) require further regeneration, which our pipeline supports.
Future work could be devoted to studying the impact on long-tail and finer-grained categories based on our protocol. (iii) NPMI as a typicality proxy. NPMI captures statistical co-occurrence regularities, not semantic or functional plausibility. Refining the typicality axis with semantic priors or human ratings is a natural follow-up. (iv) VLM / LMM mitigation. CLIP, OpenCLIP, and LLaVA-OneVision
appear in our diagnostic but not the mitigation study. Studying augmentations that lend themselves to VLM / LMM pre-training or fine-tuning is an obvious next step.

blocks.en:
Broader impacts. Co-occurrence shortcuts inflate in-distribution metrics while silently degrading behavior on under-represented compositions. Our contribution is a model-agnostic diagnostic (NPMI-paired splits, STRANGE-Bench) and a data-side mitigation (AAS) that together let practitioners measure this shortcut and, where it matters, push back. The construction recipe is general (§ C.1 ): swapping the vocabulary or co-occurrence source instantiates a fresh probe for any task family. Releasing dataset, code, and pipeline under permissive licenses (CC-BY 4.0 / MIT) is intended to lower the cost of auditing co-occurrence shortcuts in domains beyond COCO to LVIS, Objects365, fine-grained or medical vocabularies. We restrict the dataset’s intended use to evaluation to keep the distinction between probe and training distribution intact.
As with any generative-model output, STRANGE-Bench may inherit cultural or demographic biases from SD 3.5L’s training distribution, occasionally producing unintended or sensitive imagery.
